# From Slope to Area: Setting Up the Second Equation

<!-- STEP id="the-graph-again" -->
Picture the same velocity-time graph again: a straight line starting at height u, ending at height v, running for t seconds.

<!-- STEP id="recall-the-rule" -->
You already know a rule from the velocity-time graphs lesson: **the area under a velocity-time graph is the displacement.**

<!-- STEP id="shade-the-whole-thing" -->
So shade the entire area under this line, from 0 to t. That shape — flat-bottomed, with one slanted top edge — is called a **trapezium**: two parallel sides (heights u and v) joined by a slanted side.

<!-- STEP id="the-familiar-trick" -->
You've already split a shape exactly like this into two easier pieces once before — a rectangle and a triangle. Let's do it in general this time, with letters instead of numbers, and see what formula falls out.
